topics.label: Cancer therapy: lecture framing and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the class and states the lecture's subject and learning objectives before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes local treatment approaches that remove a tumor or damage it with focused radiation.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy: mechanisms, benefits, toxicity and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cytotoxic drugs damage cancer cells and the limits imposed by their effects on healthy cells and drug resistance.

topics.label: Targeting hormone dependence in breast and prostate cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes blocking hormone signals that these cancers depend on for growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cell-cycle checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how compromised checkpoint proteins can make cancer cells selectively vulnerable to irradiation or oncolytic adenoviruses.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how blocking PARP can exploit defective BRCA-mediated DNA repair to kill cancer cells.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and genome-guided target selection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how identifying cancer-driving oncogenic events can guide treatment toward the drivers on which tumor cells depend.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how kinase inhibitors target activated oncogenic kinases and how tumors can evade or become dependent on those drugs.

topics.label: Antibody-based cancer therapies
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics use antigen-binding antibodies to direct a therapeutic effect toward cells bearing a selected surface marker.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines observations that bear on whether the immune system naturally helps protect against cancer.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint inhibition and tumour neoantigens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how checkpoint blockade can restore T-cell activity and how tumor mutations may provide targets for that response.

topics.label: T-cell-engaging and CAR T-cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics describe ways to direct T cells toward cancer cells, either by bringing them together with a bispecific engager or by engineering the T cells.

topics.label: Challenges and personalised selection in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers how biomarkers, sequencing and tumor heterogeneity complicate choosing treatments for individual patients.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends and the contribution of prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers how cancer outcomes have changed and how prevention and earlier detection contribute to those trends.

topics.label: Future cancer treatment priorities and dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider how future cancer care should weigh new treatment approaches and patient welfare against the results of established therapies.
